definition: Being results-oriented is a tendency to judge work by its demonstrated outcomes rather than by activity alone.
entry_text: Being results-oriented is a tendency to judge work by its demonstrated outcomes rather than by activity alone.
example: A support lead checks whether a new help page reduced repeat questions, not just how many articles were published.
label: Results-oriented
sense_note: The adjectival label describes a work orientation.

sources.note: Deterministic sample: first four SHA-256("worker-audit-v1:" + id) per populated non-language class, excluding null definitions and root-reviewed IDs; this is not a corpus accuracy estimate. DOE Results Driven competency explicitly measures attainment of outcomes; repeat questions illustrate an outcome rather than output volume.
